verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes that the É accent must originate from the Hero V geometry and share its angles, proportions, and material language.
The client requires the shared V-and-accent geometry to move substantially farther from existing typefaces toward fully custom construction.
The client specifies that the Hero V right-arm termination will determine the É accent's terminal gesture.
The client requires the É accent to carry the Hero V's clarified right-arm gesture through its confident final stretch.
The client changes the accent rule from visual inspiration to literal extraction of the approved Hero V terminal gesture.
Target-specific implementation claim that the accent was constructed as a literal terminal slice from the approved Anchor V.
First concrete failure after the claim: the client reports visual resemblance rather than exact overlay correspondence.
Target-specific post-failure claim that the accent was rebuilt as a literal undistorted cut from the Anchor stroke.
The client strengthens the acceptance condition to exact Bézier-path duplication and perfect overlay correspondence.
Distinct integrated-wordmark failure: the client reports that the literal Hero-V relationship was lost and the accent became generic.
Target-specific post-failure claim that the generic accent was removed and the Hero V gesture was duplicated above the É.
Post-fix persistence: the client still requires direct copy/paste vector geometry instead of the interpreted or redrawn accent shown.
Target-specific claim that all presented concepts use a direct 1:1 copy/paste of the Hero V right-arm vector geometry.
The asserted change concerns preservation of locked assets across iterations, which is better owned by REQ_LOCKED_ASSET_PRESERVATION rather than the accent's derivation rule.
The client restricts the expressive Hero V right-arm signature to the Hero V and its derived É accent, excluding the remaining alphabet.
First concrete verification that the proof uses a direct, unmodified duplicate of the Hero V right-arm gesture.
The source changes how the second V is constructed and permits its optically drawn extension; it does not change the É accent's literal derivation.

The client replaces the expressive flourish with a restrained architectural terminal applied consistently to the Hero V, second V, and É accent; the obsolete expressive-exclusivity key is validly removed.
The client selects the Option B terminal baseline and requires its exact subtle reach and terminal refinements to be repeated on the É accent.
The client replaces the prior reach instruction with a very small length increase while preserving the Option B terminal geometry and removes the obsolete reach_adjustment key.
Regression after prior verification: the client reports that the exact-copy rule was unintentionally unlocked during the height study.
The client reinstates direct inheritance from the 2%-elevated Hero V master terminal and removes obsolete length and terminal-softness exploration attributes.
The client requires the restored Hero V's softer non-calligraphic terminal geometry to be transferred directly to the É accent, replacing the prior terminal treatment.
Target-specific post-modification claim that the accent now directly inherits the restored Hero V master terminal geometry.
The client makes the terminal treatment selection pending and requires the ultimately selected Hero V terminal geometry to be duplicated exactly in the É accent.
